name: E_ACT
source: O'Connor et al., "Fine-Grained DRAM", MICRO-50 2017, doi:10.1145/3123939.3124545
page/table: Table 3 (PDF p.10 of 14), row "Row activation (pJ)", HBM2 column; Sec. 4.2 text
notes: Modelled (Rambus-style floorplan model, 28 nm). Sec. 4.2: "row-activation energy, which is the sum of precharge and activate energies". 1 KB row (Table 2), 2 Gb/s/pin. 909/8192 b = 111 fJ/bit, matching Chatterjee HPCA'17 112 fJ/bit (1.8 nJ per 2 KB row). Confidence: high that the number is quoted correctly; medium as a device value (see E_ACT_meas).

name: E_PRE
notes: Included in E_ACT. Do not add a separate PRE or PREA energy, or precharge is double counted. PREA_banks_closed is not needed for energy.

name: e_preGSA
notes: Row buffer -> LDLs/MDLs -> global sense amps. Data-independent (LDL/MDL precharged to mid-rail each transfer). Matches Chatterjee HPCA'17 toggle-independent column energy 1.48 pJ/b (PDF p.8). This is the per-bit RD/WR column energy of tier 1; there is no separate RD/WR command constant.

name: e_postGSA
page/table: Table 3, "Post-GSA data movement (pJ/b)*", HBM2; footnote "* at 50% activity"
notes: GSAs -> DRAM I/O: on-die inter-bank bus to centre stripe, TSVs, base-layer wires to I/O bumps (~9.9 mm, Sec. 2.1). Toggle-dependent; value at 50% toggle.

name: e_IO
notes: Silicon-interposer channel DRAM<->GPU. Toggle-dependent; value at 50% toggle. Paid only when the GPU is off-stack (on the interposer). If the GPU sits on the HBM base die, drop it.

name: e_bit_nearbank
notes: = 386.6 pJ per 32 B transaction. Assumes the near-bank core takes data at the bank's GSAs (no inter-bank bus, TSV or I/O). Ignores the core's own short local wire.

name: E_REF_PC
source: Olgun et al., "Understanding the Power Consumption of Modern HBM...Real HBM2 DRAM Chips", arXiv:2610.14244v1, Oct 2026; artifact github.com/CMU-SAFARI/HBM-Power @c8381f74
page/table: Appendix Table 3 "All chips" row (IDD5B 696.8, IDD2N 272.7 mA); loop period from sources/fpga/.../power_measurement.cpp program_idd5 (tRFC=160 cycles at 600 MHz)
notes: (IDD5B-IDD2N)=424.1 mA over 8 PCs (PC0 of ch0-7) = 53.0 mA/PC; x 1.2 V x 266.7 ns (actual REF spacing in the loop) = 16.96 nJ. VDDC+VDDQ only (VPP not measured). If the device needs the full 350 ns, energy per REF = 22.27 nJ (upper). Rate dependence small (Table 5 slopes 0.40 vs 0.31 mA/(MT/s) per board -> ~2% lower at 1.0 Gbps). Measured on an 8-high (2 SID) 8 GB stack; whether one REF refreshes both SIDs is unknown (could halve for 4-high). Confidence: medium-low.

name: E_REFab_ch
notes: vx_phys_refresh issues one REFab per channel with PC=-1 (both pseudo-channels). Range 33.9-44.5 nJ (loop spacing vs 350 ns). Cross-check: DRAMsim3 HBM2_8Gb_x128.ini (unsourced IDDs) gives (250-55) mA x 1.2 V x 260 ns = 60.8 nJ per 128-bit channel. Refresh power at tREFI 3.9 us = 8.7 mW per channel.

name: P_PRE_SB_ch
page/table: Appendix Table 3 IDD2N 272.7 mA (all chips, 1.2 Gbps); Appendix Table 5 IDD2N board means 186.6/285.5/374.6 mA at 600/900/1200 MT/s
notes: Whole-stack idle (all banks closed, clock on) 272.7 mA at 1.2 Gbps, scaled to 1.0 Gbps with Table 5 linear fit (ratio 0.833) = 227.3 mA; /8 channels = 28.4 mA x 1.2 V = 34.1 mW per channel (17.0 mW per PC). Includes base die and the second SID share of an 8-high stack. Range 23.5 mW (Table 5 absolute, 1.0 Gbps) to 40.9 mW (Table 3 unscaled, 1.2 Gbps). VPP excluded. Confidence: medium-low (assumption: per-channel share of a stack; 8-high vs 4-high).

name: dP_ACT_SB_pc
unit: mW per pseudo-channel with >=1 open bank
page/table: Appendix Table 5 at 1200 MT/s: IDD3N1 385.7 vs IDD2N 374.6 mA per board (same 11 boards)
notes: (385.7-374.6)/2 chips/8 PCs x 1.2 V = 0.83 mW. Slopes equal (0.31 mA/(MT/s)), so the same at 1.0 Gbps. Appendix Table 3 gives IDD3N1 (231.8) < IDD2N (272.7), i.e. not resolvable; the increment is within noise. Per extra open bank: (IDD3N16-IDD3N1)/(15x8) x 1.2 V = 0.15 mW. Sensitivity alternative: DRAMsim3 (IDD3N-IDD2N)=15 mA per 128-bit channel -> 9 mW per PC. Confidence: low; small either way.

name: E_ACT_meas
source: Olgun et al. arXiv:2610.14244; loop from power_measurement.cpp program_idd0
page/table: Appendix Table 3 (IDD0 309.7, IDD3N1 231.8, IDD2N 272.7 mA); loop = 1 ACT+PRE per 28 cycles (46.7 ns) per PC, 8 PCs
notes: Consistency check only. Background weighted 0.75 x IDD3N1 + 0.25 x IDD2N (bank open 21 of 28 cycles) -> dI = 67.7 mA/8 PCs -> 474 pJ. Sensitive to the background choice: 259 pJ (IDD2N) to 545 pJ (IDD3N1); Table 5 board means give 906 pJ. So measured ACT energy lies in 0.26-0.91 nJ, VPP excluded; O'Connor's 909 pJ is at the top of that range.

name: e_RD_meas
page/table: Appendix Table 3 IDD4R 2881.0, IDD3N16 246.9 mA; 8 PCs x 64 b x 1.2 Gb/s = 614.4 Gb/s
notes: Consistency check only: (2881.0-246.9) mA x 1.2 V / 614.4 Gb/s, assuming 100% bus use in the loop (if lower, per-bit is higher). All-0s read (1717.9 mA, artifact config note) -> 2.87 pJ/b. O'Connor full path 3.48 pJ/b at 50% toggle, so it is likely low for reads; the paper reports FGDRAM-model MAPE 20-23%.

name: e_WR_meas
notes: Consistency check only. DRAM side only: on writes the GPU PHY drives the channel, which is not in this number.

name: tRFC
source: Ramulator2 HBM2.cpp tRFC_TABLE (2Gb 160, 4Gb 260, 8Gb 350, 16Gb 450 ns); vortex sim/common/dram_sim.cpp shadow nRFC=ceil(350/tick_ns)
notes: JESD235D not checked (paywalled). 2Gb=160 ns and 4Gb=260 ns agree with gem5 hbm.py and gthparch/HBM; I found no public primary source for 8Gb=350 ns (gem5 HBM_1000_4H_1x64 uses 260 ns for 8Gb dies, DRAMsim3 HBM2_8Gb uses 260 ns, and the Olgun loop uses 266.7 ns while its comment says "tRFC=350ns"). Confidence: medium. Affects timing only; energy uses E_REF.

name: tREFI
source: Olgun et al. arXiv:2610.14244 Sec. 2.2 citing JEDEC JESD235D (2021); gem5 hbm.py

name: VDD
source: Olgun et al. Sec. 4.1 (VDDC and VDDQ 1.2 V); DRAMsim3 HBM2 ini
notes: VPP (2.5 V) not covered by any measured number here.
